PATIENTS WITH SIGNS OF INFECTION MORE THAN 48 HOURS AFTER PROCEDURE Most post-operative infections appear at least 4 days after the operation.  If the wound appears normal to examination surgical site infection is unlikely.

Seek other source of fever.  Consider opening wounds that show induration or erythema.  Obtain material for gram stain and culture whenever possible.

Determine whether the patient has signs of invasive or systemic infection like erythema (diameter greater than 5 centimeters), temperature greater than 38.5 degrees Celsius (101.3 degrees Fahrenheit) or heart rate higher than 100 beats per minute.

If there are no signs of invasive or systemic infection systemic antimicrobials are unnecessary.  Dressing changes alone are indicated.

# For wounds that require complicated care

Place wound care consult.

If there are signs of invasive or systemic infection obtain blood cultures and wound Gram stain and cultures.  Whenever possible select antimicrobial therapy based on the Gram stain.  When the Gram stain cannot provide guidance give empirical therapy as indicated:

[References](references)

Stevens DL Clin Infect Dis 2014, 59: 147
Therapy:
## Empirical treatment of INFECTED WOUNDS AFTER CLEAN SURGERY or wounds on the trunk, head, neck, arms or legs

Vancomycin should be included in the initial regimen due to the prevalence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.  However beta-lactam antibiotics are more effective for susceptible bacteria than is vancomycin.  If methicillin-susceptible S. aureus is identified switch to an anti-staphylococcal beta-lactam antibiotic.

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) R

## Preferred empirical treatment for INFECTED WOUNDS AFTER CLEAN-CONTAMINATED or

## CONTAMINATED SURGERY

Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h ($$) R < OR >

Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h ($) R,DI <AND> Clindamycin 600 mg IV
q8h ($$) [H]

## Alternative if methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is suspected

Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h ($$) R <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg

IV q12h ($) [R] < OR >
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h ($) R,DI <AND> metronidazole 500 mg

IV q8h ($) [DI] <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12 ($) [R]
